_doc: Slice B0 — THE LENS CONFIG. Instrument = MOOD LENS (user's choice) x ROLE,
shaded by the star's real colour (B-V). Never per-object.
This file is the single source of truth for both consumers: the live app
(src/engine/audio/samplerLenses.ts, which types and validates it) and the
offline renderer (scripts/render-score.mjs). Keeping it as data, not code,
is what stops the two from drifting apart.
Switching lenses must NEVER change pitches or timing — only timbre. Every
role in every lens therefore covers the same MIDI range; where a lens's
first-choice instrument cannot reach a note within `maxShiftSemitones`, the
bank falls through to the next instrument in the list.
`gainDb` is a per-lens voicing offset applied BEFORE the mix law's stem
trims, so it shapes the blend inside a role without moving the stem target.
Five lenses per MUSICAL_VISION.md section 5.
The B-V hook. Every event already carries `timbre.{warmth,brightness}`,
derived by the mapping layer from the star's real B-V colour index.
Here that becomes a spectral tilt: a hot blue star (brightness -> 1) is
voiced brighter, a cool red one (warmth -> 1) darker. Same sample, same
pitch, same time — only the colour of the tone moves.
`tiltDb` is the full-scale swing applied at brightness 0 vs 1 by a
one-pole shelf hinged at `hingeHz`. Kept modest on purpose: this is
shading, not an effect.

_doc: THE MASTERING LAW (Slice B1) — extends the mix law with the two things a
musician's review found missing: spectral separation, and loudness.
The mix law sets how LOUD each role is. It says nothing about WHERE each
role sits in the spectrum, so five roles can hit their targets and still
pile into the same 200-800 Hz band — which is what makes a mix sound
'muddy' even when every fader is right. The EQ lanes below carve the
sustained pads (ground, chord) where the moving parts (figuration, lead)
actually live, so motion is heard rather than merely measured.
Loudness is normalised to a LUFS target rather than to peak. Peak
normalisation rewards crest factor, not loudness: the B0 clips needed a
shared -11.8 dB fader precisely because per-clip peak matching would have
printed them 9 dB apart. -18 LUFS is the ambient/background target here —
well under streaming's -14, because this is music to leave running, and
loud is the opposite of what it is for.
The limiter stays a safety device. If it engages at all, something upstream
is wrong; the checker asserts 0% engagement.
RATIFIED AMENDMENT, 2026-08-10. The original law said the limiter must never
engage at all. Measured, that rule and the -18 LUFS target could not both be
met: figuration's crest factor after RMS matching is about 29 dB, so peak-
guarding alone left lenses up to 8.9 dB under target — an 8 dB spread between
lenses, which is exactly what normalising to loudness was introduced to
remove.
HQ's read, ratified by Shambu: the 0% rule was written to protect the
SUSTAINED bed's breathing, not to forbid transient control — which is what
limiters are for. So limiting is now permitted on transients only, and the
protection it was written for is asserted directly instead of by proxy:
ZERO gain reduction on the ground and chord stems, structurally, because the
limiters live on the figuration and lead stems and the bed has none.
RATIFIED BY HQ, 2026-09-01 (Slice B2). `maxEngagedFraction` is raised from
0.01 to 0.10, for the transient-carrying stems only. The 1% figure predates
any measurement of struck figuration: it is the original 0% rule scaled down
by intuition rather than derived from an observation. Measured, a kalimba or
glockenspiel weave engages a 3 dB look-ahead limiter on 1.2-8.7% of samples,
and every one of those catches is at or under the ratified 3 dB ceiling.
That is glue on a percussive layer, not squash: the REDUCTION bound is what
protects the transient, and the engagement fraction only ever said how often
a bounded reduction happens.
What is NOT relaxed, and is why this is safe: the bed. Ground and chord stay
at ZERO engagement, structurally, because they have no limiter at all. The
0% rule was written to protect the sustained bed's breathing, and that is
still protected by construction rather than by a number.
`zeroEngagementStems` is the operative half of this law.
RATIFIED BY HQ, 2026-09-04 (Slice B3). 0.10 -> 0.15, transient-carrying
stems only. Post-fix figuration on struck material engages the look-ahead
limiter more often than the pre-fix measurement showed, and on struck
material the engagement FRACTION tracks note density rather than squash:
a kalimba weave asks the limiter for a bounded catch on every strike.
Depth is the audible constraint, and depth is unchanged at 3.0 dB.
HQ NOTES FOR THE RECORD that this number has now moved twice and that both
earlier values were set before anyone had measured post-fix figuration. It
should not move a third time without evidence that something is AUDIBLE.
The bed stays at ZERO, structurally, as it has since 2026-08-10.
Gentle bus compression on FIGURATION ONLY. The figuration's velocities are
magnitude-derived and span a wide range within a single movement; a slow,
shallow squeeze evens the weave without touching the macro arc.
Nothing else is compressed. The 11-minute build from one star to the bloom
is the composition — flattening it would undo Slice A4.
`maxReductionDb` is ENFORCED by the compressor, not merely implied by the
threshold and ratio. Measured on the aurora steady state, threshold -26 with
ratio 2 reached 7.4 dB of reduction once the stem was correctly trimmed onto
its -19 dBFS target — settings that satisfy a law at one level do not satisfy
it at another. The threshold below sits just under the trimmed stem's peaks
so the device does real work, and the clamp guarantees it stays glue.
`releaseSeconds` is 1.0 and not the 1.2 first written, because Web Audio's
DynamicsCompressorNode caps release at 1 second: the live graph threw on
construction. The offline glue has no such limit and would happily have run
at 1.2 — which is exactly the wrong outcome. A law the two paths implement
differently is not one law, so the number moved to what both can honour.
What the EQ lanes claim, stated so it can be MEASURED IN THE AUDIO.
An earlier form of this asked how much of a pad's energy sits in the motion
band relative to the pad's own level, and it was the wrong question: a violin
section genuinely has most of its energy at 700-5000 Hz, so the number said
'muddy' about a mix that was fine and would have gone on saying it however
deep the carve went.
The claim the lanes actually make is comparative — IN THE BAND WHERE THE
FIGURATION SINGS, THE FIGURATION IS IN FRONT. `minMotionLeadDb` is set at the
meaningful threshold (in front, not behind) rather than fitted to today's
measurement, which on the aurora steady state is +13.3 dB over ground and
+1.8 dB over chord.
